summary: Equity closed at $600.92 (day -$3.82, -0.6%, drawdown 0.6% from peak), against SPY -0.85% over the same window since 10-20 and the fully invested shadow book at +1.55%. The three approved buys (VRSN $25, BND $30, VOO $15) all filled at the open and closed near cost: BND -0.1%, VOO new lot flat (the whole VOO position is -0.9% because of the older 10-20 lot), VRSN +3.7%. Cash is about $125 (21% of equity), as planned. The calls held up on their reasoning. Cutting VRSN from $35 to $25 because the post-print reaction was unseen was sensible: it filled at $292.23, 4.7% under the $306.48 menu close, so the stock did gap down after the print, then recovered to about $303. L1 (anchor the stop to the actual fill) mattered here, since a stop built from the menu close would have sat about 14% below the fill instead of 10%. Dropping IEF kept the rate bet to one $30 position through a day when BND only slipped 0.2%, and rejecting MTCH kept Technology off a day when tech was sold (CARG -3.7%). I cannot grade MTCH or IEF because close.json carries no prices for rejected names. The weak point is pace: the owner wants the account mostly invested within about a week of 10-20, 21% cash with four trading days left is still behind, and the shadow book's lead today is mostly the cost of that idle cash plus its larger bond and international sleeves, not evidence the picks were wrong. One day of P&L is not a verdict on any of these calls. No thesis is broken at the close.
lessons: L1 held up. VRSN filled 4.7% below its pre-print menu close, so a stop copied from the menu close would have been far wider than the intended 10%. Keep writing stops as a percentage of the actual fill and check the gap direction as well as the gap size, since gaps down after a print matter as much as gaps up.

Staging a smaller size into an unseen post-earnings reaction worked: VRSN was bought at $25 instead of $35, gapped down at the open and recovered. Keep trimming sizes when the reaction to a fresh print is not in the inputs, but do not go to zero when the fundamentals rank is clear.

Pace risk: cash is still about 21% of equity with the owner's one-week target ending around 10-27. Next session, weigh unspent cash as a cost explicitly. Prefer unheld, event-clear names and non-duplicate ETF sleeves over adding to VOO or VTI, and keep avoiding two near-identical bond funds before the Fed meeting.

Watch list for next run: the Fed meeting next week (BND stop is 2% under the fill), IDXX earnings estimated 11-02 after a Jefferies price-target cut, WMT momentum that commentators call stretched, and staples at about 22% of equity (DPZ's staples label is a data artifact, but WMT and KR are real staples exposure). Do not add to staples without a reason beyond the sector view.
